attachments.insertion_landmark: spinous processes T1-T8 (thoracis); C7/ligamentum nuchae to axis spinous process (cervicis, frequently rudimentary)

functional_compartments.name: Spinalis thoracis
functional_compartments.function_note: Smallest, most medial erector spinae column; spans spinous process to spinous process, adding little independent moment arm beyond longissimus/iliocostalis.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Spinalis cervicis
functional_compartments.function_note: Frequently thin, variable, or absent; spinalis capitis (when present) is usually inseparable from semispinalis capitis rather than a discrete belly, a well-documented anatomical variant pattern.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Linear (or curvilinear in larger patients) probe in parasagittal orientation, 2-3 cm lateral to the spinous process at the target thoracic level (T5 in the original description of the block).
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: As the most medial column of the erector spinae group, this muscle is one of the layers the needle passes through en route to the transverse process during an erector spinae plane (ESP) block -- though at the standard 2-3 cm parasagittal window it is often difficult to resolve individually from the adjacent longissimus and multifidus. Local anesthetic is deposited deep to the erector spinae mass (including this muscle), superficial to the transversospinalis muscles.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Hyperechoic tip of the transverse process contacted by the needle; visible linear anechoic spread lifting the erector spinae muscle mass (including this muscle) off the transverse process/transversospinalis muscles on injection.
structures_at_risk: dorsal and ventral rami of the spinal nerves near the transverse process -- the likely site of action per the original cadaveric/CT dye-spread study
pleura, if the needle is walked laterally off the transverse process (the classic technique avoids this by stopping at bone contact)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: No motor-point/neural-arborization mapping for BoNT injection into this muscle's own belly was found -- consistent with this atlas's established finding for the erector spinae group (see the iliocostalis entries) that deep paraspinal motor-point data is genuinely sparse compared to limb muscles. What is well documented is the erector spinae plane (ESP) block, whose needle path passes through this muscle (as part of the erector spinae mass) before depositing local anesthetic deep to it; included here because it is the real clinical ultrasound technique relevant to this muscle's location, not a claim of a motor point within it.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Forero M, Adhikary SD, Lopez H, Tsui C, Chin KJ (2016) 'The Erector Spinae Plane Block: A Novel Analgesic Technique in Thoracic Neuropathic Pain', Reg Anesth Pain Med 41(5):621-627, doi:10.1097/AAP.0000000000000451 -- original description of the block, including cadaveric/CT dye-spread investigation of its likely site of action
